description: Flag new dependencies or approaches that diverge from `docs/TECH_STACK.md` without justification.
If the PR claims to fix a bug, verify the code actually addresses the root cause.
If the PR adds a feature, verify the implementation matches the described scope.
Flag scope creep - changes unrelated to the stated purpose belong in separate PRs.

Compare the ClickUp task description and acceptance criteria against the PR's actual changes. Flag significant scope gaps where the PR clearly misses stated acceptance criteria or implements something materially different from the ticket. Do not flag minor wording differences.
If the ticket is already marked as done/closed but this PR is still open, flag as warning - possible stale PR or ticket updated prematurely.
When reviewing feature code, check existing `docs/features/` for how the feature should work. Flag deviations from documented design unless the docs are also updated in the same PR.
Flag PRs that update feature docs without corresponding code changes - docs should not drift ahead of implementation.

Check if the PR modifies files in `openspec/changes/<name>/` (especially `tasks.md` with checked-off tasks). If implementation tasks are complete but the change directory is NOT moved to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`, the archive step was skipped.

Check for delta specs at `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` that should have been synced to `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`. If deltas exist in the active change but the canonical specs were not updated, spec sync was skipped.
If the PR is a spec-only PR (PR1 - only adds/modifies OpenSpec artifacts, no runtime code), archival is NOT expected. Archival happens in the implementation PR (PR2).
If the PR does not touch any OpenSpec change files and is not linked to a change, this check does not apply.
